heading_en: Market Risk Equivalent Amount for Default Risk
summary_ja: DRCモデルによるデフォルト・リスクに対するマーケット・リスク相当額の算出方法、DRCモデルの要件（信頼水準、保有期間、相関、PD・LGD等）、管理規程・検証・ベンチマークを定める。
summary_en: Sets how the market risk equivalent amount for default risk is calculated using the DRC model, the requirements for the DRC model (confidence level, holding period, correlations, PD, LGD, etc.), and governance, validation and benchmarking.
paragraphs: An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall use the DRC model to calculate the market risk equivalent amount for default risk relating to credit products and equities in trading desks.

The market risk equivalent amount for default risk shall be the larger of the following amounts calculated by the DRC model. (i) The amount based on the most recent measurement; (ii) The amount based on the average of the measurements over the most recent 12 weeks.

The DRC model shall satisfy all of the following requirements. (i) The credit value at risk relating to default risk (meaning the maximum loss expected within a certain probability range due to the default of a future obligor or issuer of equities, etc. (hereinafter in this paragraph referred to as "obligor, etc."), assuming that a specific position is held for a certain period (referred to as the "holding period" in item (v))) shall be measured weekly at a one-tailed 99.9 percent confidence level; (ii) A default simulation model (meaning a model that estimates the loss given obligor default (excluding losses due to rating downgrades of the obligor prior to default)) using two types of systematic risk factors shall be used; (iii) Default correlations relating to obligors, etc. shall be estimated on the basis of credit spreads or the prices of listed equities; (iv) The estimation under the preceding item shall be based on data covering at least 10 years (including the stress period); (v) The holding period shall be assumed to be one year; provided, however, that in the case of an equity portfolio, it may be assumed to be 60 days; (vi) Equity positions shall be modelled so that the issuer's default is assumed to bring the share price to zero; (vii) Default risk shall be measured for each obligor, etc.; (viii) Default risk shall take into account the loss arising at default in addition to the valuation gain or loss as of the valuation date; (ix) Where an obligor, etc. defaults, the additional loss that it is expected to incur, relative to the current mark-to-market valuation, shall be calculated for all positions concerned; (x) The effect of the business cycle shall be reflected in the loss amounts assumed by the model; (xi) Long exposures to the same obligor, etc. and the corresponding short exposures shall be offset. In this case, where the exposures include different instruments relating to the same obligor, etc., the seniority and subordination among those different instruments, etc. shall be taken into account; (xii) Basis risk between long exposures and short exposures to different obligors, etc. shall be included in the model. In this case, offsetting of default risk between long exposures and short exposures spanning different obligors, etc. shall be carried out through the modelling of default risk; (xiii) Positions shall not be offset before being input to the model; (xiv) Default correlations among different obligors, etc. shall satisfy all of the following requirements: (a) Correlations shall be based on objective data, and the level of correlations shall not be arbitrarily adjusted on the basis of the composition of its own positions; (b) The appropriateness of the correlation modelling method for its own portfolio and of the selection of systematic risk factors shall be verified. In this case, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall prepare documentation concerning that method; (c) Correlations shall assume a holding period of one year or more; (d) All material basis risks shall be reflected in the correlations; (xv) All material mismatches arising between positions and their hedges shall be captured; (xvi) The effect of concentration in specific obligors, etc. or markets during the stress period shall be appropriately taken into account for all types of instruments; (xvii) The effect of non-linear risk relating to options and other positions shall be reflected; (xviii) Where a simplified model is used for equity derivative positions with multiple underlying assets, the approval of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency shall be obtained; (xix) The PD input to the model shall have a floor of 0.03 percent, and where estimates used for the internal ratings-based approach for credit risk exist, those estimates shall be used, while where such estimates do not exist, a PD satisfying all of the following requirements shall be calculated; provided, however, that where such estimates do not exist, this floor need not be applied to exposures for which a risk weight of zero percent is permitted under Articles 22 through 24 and Article 26, paragraph (3): (a) Market-price-based PD shall not be used; provided, however, that this does not apply where approval of the Commissioner of the Financial Services Agency has been obtained for such use; (b) PD based on observed historical default experience shall be used; provided, however, that an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach may use theoretical-value-based PD where it can substantiate that it does not deviate from PD based on historical default experience; (c) Where the level of PD is adjusted on the basis of data on securities listed on an exchange, the observation period shall be at least five years, including a business cycle; (d) Where PD provided by an external data source is used, it shall be substantiated that it is relevant to its own portfolio; (xx) The LGD input to the model shall use, where estimates used for the internal ratings-based approach for credit risk exist, those estimates, while where such estimates do not exist, an LGD satisfying all of the following requirements shall be calculated: (a) It shall be calculated on the basis of the amount obtained by subtracting the expected market value of the position at the time of default from the current market value of the position; (b) It shall reflect the type of position and the seniority and subordination structure; provided, however, that where it falls below zero, it shall be zero; (c) It shall be based on sufficient historical data; (d) Where LGD provided by an external data source is used, it shall be substantiated that it is relevant to its own portfolio; (xxi) The order of priority in obtaining PD and LGD shall be established, and they shall not be selected arbitrarily.

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall establish in writing, for the DRC model, the management rules necessary for its proper operation (including the requirements for the use of credit spreads or share prices, correlations, and management procedures for PD and LGD (including level adjustment and validation)).

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall evaluate the DRC model by stress tests, sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis or other similar methods. In this case, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall carry out validation assuming events drawn from past experience and other events.
An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall construct a benchmark for evaluating the overall accuracy of the DRC model.
An Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the internal model approach shall put in place specific validation procedures for the validation of the DRC model.
A trading desk that calculates the market risk equivalent amount using the DRC model shall calculate the market risk equivalent amount using expected shortfall or stressed expected shortfall.
